title: Object and Edit Mode - Blender 2.80 Fundamentals
annotator: DRAFT derived from a user-supplied transcript (auto-captions via a third-party tool) by Claude; NOT yet checked against the video by a human

steps.goal: Enter Edit Mode by changing the mode drop-down menu in the top-left corner of the 3D viewport
steps.note: narration at 0:22.8-0:26.6; dropdown label/location to be confirmed visually

steps.goal: Press Tab to toggle between Edit Mode and Object Mode (hotkey alternative)
steps.note: a toggle: resulting mode depends on the previous mode, so no single expected state

steps.goal: While in Edit Mode manipulate vertices, edges and faces to change the shape of the mesh (stated, not yet demonstrated)
steps.note: general statement; the demonstration comes at step 5

steps.goal: Toggle back into Object Mode to move the object as a whole
steps.note: narrated as a general rule; actually performed at step 6

steps.goal: In Edit Mode change the cube into a random shape by selecting one or more vertices and moving, rotating or scaling them with the transform tools
steps.note: narration at 0:58.9-1:08.5; exact tool clicks must be read off the screen

steps.goal: Toggle back into Object Mode with Tab
Rotate the cube in Object Mode to add an action to the undo history
Press Ctrl+Z to undo and see that the Edit Mode undo history is still intact
steps.note: which state results (mode, shape) must be read off the screen; left empty on purpose

steps.goal: Select all the mesh objects you want to edit and enter Edit Mode to edit several objects at once
steps.note: narration 2:00.0-2:06.5; hotkey vs menu entry not stated for this step

steps.goal: Try to connect vertices of two separate objects with F (Fill): Blender refuses
In Object Mode select both objects and join them with Object > Join
steps.note: mode alone does not show a join happened; the object count would

steps.goal: Alternative: press Ctrl+J to join the selected objects
Enter Edit Mode and select a part of the mesh
Choose Mesh > Separate > Selection to split the selected geometry into a new object
steps.note: result is a new object; not expressible in the current predicate vocabulary
